name: GA-05
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Nikema Williams running for reelection
Republican challenger has no reported fundraising
model.rationale: Atlanta-based GA-05 carries a D+36 lean, and incumbent Nikema Williams is running with a solid fundraising edge while her Republican opponent shows no reported money. Prediction markets price a Democratic win at 99%, and no evidence suggests a competitive race.
model.watch: Only an extraordinary, unforeseen scandal or candidate collapse would put this seat in play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Georgia's 5th District, centered on Atlanta, is one of the most Democratic-leaning House seats in the country, with a partisan lean of D+36. Incumbent Nikema Williams is seeking reelection and has raised about $600,000, while Republican challenger John Oscar Salvesen reports no fundraising. No public polls or expert ratings exist for the race, and no outside spending has been reported.

Prediction markets give Williams a 99% chance of winning, consistent with the district's fundamentals. With no polling, the forecast rests on the district's heavy Democratic lean, incumbency, and the financial mismatch, all pointing to a comfortable Democratic hold with wide but standard uncertainty for a race lacking survey data.
